name: Distal Radius Fracture Rehabilitation

blocks.text: The distal radius fracture is one of the most common fractures, especially in older women with osteoporosis after a fall on the outstretched hand. A Colles fracture has dorsal displacement of the fragment; a Smith fracture has palmar displacement. Treatment is casting (often around 6 weeks) or surgical fixation, usually a volar plate. Physiotherapy restores movement, strength and function, and screens for complications.

sections.title: B. Recognize the presentation after immobilisation

items: Stiff wrist and forearm (especially supination and extension), stiff fingers if not exercised.
Weak grip, swelling, pain with loading.

rows: How was it treated, and when did the cast come off or surgery happen?
Any burning pain, colour or temperature change, extreme sensitivity?
Numbness in thumb, index and middle fingers?
Pain at the thumb side when extending the thumb?

blocks.text: Inspection (swelling, colour, sweating, skin and nail changes), finger range (composite fist), wrist range, forearm supination and pronation, grip strength, sensation, ulnar-side wrist pain (TFCC, distal radio-ulnar joint), function (PRWE questionnaire).

rows: Combination of sensory, vasomotor, sudomotor and motor or trophic signs out of proportion to the injury
Supports CRPS diagnosis by a doctor [Ref – to verify criteria]
Weakness or inability to lift the thumb off a table
Tenderness between ulnar styloid and flexor carpi ulnaris
Finger stiffness must be addressed early

sections.title: F to G. Differential diagnosis and red flags

rows: Rapid swelling, numbness, severe pain in cast
Disproportionate burning pain, colour and temperature change, sweating
Sudden inability to extend the thumb

steps: **During immobilisation:** finger, elbow and shoulder movement.
**After cast or early after volar plate:** active range, then strengthening.

rows: Dorsal glide for flexion, palmar glide for extension, grades III to IV
Fingertips toward the elbow, with elevation
Tendon gliding, thumb opposition, shoulder and elbow range, elevation
Active wrist flexion and extension, radial and ulnar deviation, forearm rotation with a hammer, composite fist
Putty grip, wrist curls with light weight, weight-bearing through the hand on a table
Carrying, opening jars, push-up progressions, work and hobby tasks

blocks.text: Heat before exercise for stiffness; contrast baths not essential. Splints may be used for support or for stretching stiff joints as advised.

sections.title: L to M. Management and reassessment

blocks.text: Track wrist and forearm range, grip strength (percentage of other side), PRWE. Refer older patients for bone health and falls prevention (Vol 11 Ch 4 and 5).

items: **Why move the fingers during casting?** To prevent finger stiffness and swelling, which are major causes of poor outcome.
**What is CRPS and why act early?** A disproportionate pain condition with vasomotor and trophic changes; early recognition and graded activity improve outcomes.
**Which motion is often slowest to return?** Supination and wrist extension.
**Sudden inability to lift the thumb weeks after fracture?** Possible EPL rupture; refer.
**What else should an older patient receive?** Falls prevention and bone health assessment.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Plan rehabilitation for each phase after distal radius fracture.
Screen for CRPS, nerve and tendon complications.
Use joint mobilisation and progressive loading safely.

sections.A: Kalai ke paas radius haddi ka fracture bohat aam hai, khaas kar osteoporosis wali bari umar ki khawateen mein haath ke bal girne se.
sections.B: Plaster ke baad kalai aur forearm akde hue (khaas kar supination aur extension), ungliyan akdi, grip kamzor.
sections.C: Kaise ilaaj hua, plaster kab utra ya surgery kab hui, aur kya jalan wala dard, rang ya garmi ki tabdeeli hai (CRPS).
sections.D: Sujan, rang aur paseena dekhein, mutthi, kalai aur forearm ki range aur grip napein.
sections.E: CRPS ke liye Budapest criteria aur nerve aur tendon ke complications screen karein.
sections.F: Plaster mein tezi se sujan, sunn-pan aur shadeed dard (emergency), aur CRPS, angoothe ka tendon phatna aur haddi ka dobara khisakna (urgent).
sections.H: Surgeon ki hidayat aur healing phase dekhein, complications screen karein, phir phase ke mutabiq exercise.
sections.I: Haddi judne ke baad akdan rahe to kalai ke joints aur forearm ke jor ki glides.
sections.J: Plaster mein ungliyan, angootha, kohni aur kandha chalte rahein. Plaster utarne ke baad active range, phir taaqat.
sections.K: Akdan mein exercise se pehle garmi. Splint support ya stretch ke liye.
sections.L: Kalai aur forearm ki range, grip aur PRWE track karein. Bari umar ke patients ko haddiyon ki sehat aur girne se bachao ke liye refer karein.
sections.N: Sawaal hal karein. Plaster ke dauraan ungliyan hilana zaroori hai taa ke akdan aur sujan na ho.
sections.now-you-should-be-able-to: Yeh checklist hai. Har point khud kar sakein to tick karein.
